page.overview:
Who is Alcoholic?

The Alcoholic, the Man with a Bottle or the Drunk is a recurring character who has brief appearances in three Roger Moore-era Bond films, played by Victor Tourjansky. The character is a comic foil to James Bond, reacting to his antics and looking at his bottle in disbelief. The man's nationality is unclear, but since he turns up in three separate tourist areas of Italy, this may indicate he is Italian.

In the Spy Who Loved Me, we see the man for the first time sitting on a crowded family beach on the coast of Sardinia. He is enjoying a tipple when he witnesses James Bond's amphibious Lotus Esprit emerging from the Mediterranean.

This time the man is on the Piazza San Marco (St. Mark's Square), an even busier area in Venice. He is at a table, enjoying a meal, surrounded by tourists. When James Bond goes by on his gondola hovercraft, he displays complete astonishment, as do all of his neighbours which include a nearby dog and a double-taking pigeon.

In the briefest of his appearances, the man is at an Alpine ski resort, and again sees James Bond going by. He is dressed partly in skiing gear, so he is probably on holiday again.
